s02.translation: May Thy Body, O Lord, which I have received, and the Blood which I have drunk, cleave to my inmost parts:

s03.translation: and grant that no stain of sins remain in me, whom pure and holy sacraments have refreshed:

s04.translation: Who livest and reignest for ever and ever. Amen.

s05.narrative: The priest washes and dries his fingers, consumes the ablution, wipes his mouth and the chalice, folds the corporal, covers the chalice, replaces it on the altar, and then continues the Mass.

w001.function: The first of the two subjects of “adhǽreat” (w010), which is singular.

w010.function: Viscéribus is read as a plural dative: the Body and Blood are to “cleave to my inmost parts”.

w014.function: Imperative governing the clause introduced by “ut” (w015).

w022.function: Masculine singular relative pronoun referring to “me” (w017), not feminine “mácula” (w021) or neuter plural “sacraménta” (w027).
